theme.verified: All eight source files matched the GitHub git-tree blob IDs before local adaptation.

local_changes.site.js: Show the real static logo image when paused or reduced, switch to the native-controls video only on actual playback, synchronize native pause with the accessible global motion button, and retain readable still/retry on autoplay rejection.
local_changes.style.css: Allow the media-action links to wrap without overflowing narrow screens. Honor hidden on the static-image/video pair so native controls cannot obscure the paused logo.
local_changes.family.json: Add Foley under robotdad; preserve every existing family entry.
local_changes.build.py: Expose the shared motion toggle on static tool pages too. Give Foley's transparent poster a validated dark media background, label its video as animation, and link the static logo and artwork provenance. Include the MIT notice as assets/theme-LICENSE.txt in generated output. Apply repository Ruff formatting, rename an ambiguous reader-loop variable, and guard missing/non-string reader hrefs to satisfy the repository type check. The actual upstream tool-page template and shared presentation are retained.

theme.shared_artwork: The existing family mark remains separate from Foley branding. Upstream identifies artwork provenance in amplifier-smart-tools/site/artwork; this copy does not claim independent artwork review.

workflow.adaptations: Remove catalog refresh triggers and fork-family override; keep PR builds read-only, deploy only main push or explicit main dispatch, and add structural checks. The tool-page build needs only Python standard library, so no build dependency installation is needed.

publication: Enable GitHub Pages with GitHub Actions only after preview approval; allow main in the github-pages environment. Main pushes touching site or workflow then deploy automatically.

foley_media.status: Actual Unfold-generated logo and animation integrated; not a Foley audio demonstration.
foley_media.integration: 1186x284 transparent PNG and silent four-second H.264 MP4. The dark #111820 media background preserves the white wordmark contrast. Shared template reduced-motion and global motion controls are retained.
